lesson.title: Your Approach Shapes Your First Volley
lesson.hook: Before blaming your hands, inspect the first volley your approach gives you.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you approach, compare their contact position with your first-volley height.

pro.label: Federer v Murray, Dubai 2012 final
pro.moment: Coach Mike Crooks's frame-by-frame: Federer follows the line of his approach as he comes in, two running steps covering a lot of court, and plays the first volley well inside the service box.
pro.read: Your first volley inherits the approach.

drill.name: Follow it in
drill.how: Approach deep and follow the line of your own ball. Your first volley must be played inside the service line. Your partner passes or lobs as they like.

steps.name: Short forehand, line open
steps.sit: You're balanced on a short forehand. Their recovery leaves the line open.
steps.q: Which approach sets up your volley?
opts: Short through the middle, come in
Deep down the line, come in
Float it deep through the middle, come in
steps.payoff: A deep approach keeps them back while you move in.
steps.principle: Your approach decides how hard your first volley will be.
steps.why: A short approach lets them hit from inside the court. Deep, they're passing from behind the baseline, and you get an easier volley.
steps.take: Approach deep and follow it in: their contact goes back, your volley up.

lines.A: Short through the middle — they step in and pass you.
lines.B: Deep down the line keeps them back — you put the volley away.
lines.C: Short angle — they run it down and pass you crosscourt.
lines.D: A floater — they step in and drive it past you.

steps.name: The short line approach
steps.sit: Your down-the-line approach lands short, and they pass you. Watch it.
steps.payoff: Deeper, and their pass starts from further back.
steps.principle: If you're getting passed, check your approach before your volley.
steps.why: The short approach let them hit an early, low pass. Getting closer or hitting harder doesn't change where they hit from; depth does.
steps.take: Passed at the net? Look at the approach first: add depth, keep margin.

lines.A: Same short landing, one stride closer — they still pass you.
lines.B: Sharper and still short — they get there and pass you.
lines.C: More pace from that length — into the net.
lines.D: Deeper — a slower pass, and you put the volley away.

steps.name: Backhand side, line covered
steps.sit: Now you approach from your backhand side. They're already covering the line.
opts: Short down the line, come in
Short through the middle, come in
Deep down the line, come in
steps.payoff: They covered the line, so the deep crosscourt made them travel.
steps.principle: Approach deep, to where they aren't, not to a fixed side.
steps.why: The rule was never 'always down the line'. It's deep, and away from them. Follow the ball's direction so both passes are covered.
steps.take: They cover the line? Go deep across and follow the ball's direction.

lines.A: Deep crosscourt makes them travel — too far for them.
lines.B: Short down the line into their position — they pass you.
lines.C: Short through the middle — they step in and pass you.
lines.D: Deep line, straight to them — you only just dig out a low volley.
